onboarding.intro: These numbers feed the Mifflin-St Jeor equation for your BMR, then your training frequency sets the multiplier for TDEE. Your daily calorie and macro targets update live as you type.
onboarding.birthDateHint: Age is part of the BMR equation.
onboarding.sectionMacrosHint: How your calories divide into protein, carbs and fat. Pick what suits how you like to eat — you can change it any time.
onboarding.coachFormulaHint: Protein pinned to your bodyweight ({proteinPerKg} g/kg for your goal), fat at 25% of calories, carbs fill the rest. Protein-forward — heavier than some people want.
onboarding.customSplitHint: Set your own percentages — they just need to total 100.
onboarding.splitInvalid: Currently {sum}% — the three must total 100% ({min}–{max}% each).
onboarding.changeLater: You can change all of this later.
onboarding.completeToUnlock: Complete all three sections to unlock.
onboarding.sexHint: It's used only for the BMR equation: Mifflin-St Jeor adds 5 for male and subtracts 161 for female.
onboarding.under18: Tracking works the same for you. The AI coach is available from age 18.
onboarding.ageHint: Your age comes from your date of birth, so it stays right as the years go by.

hero.title: Your day, in <grad>one orbit.</grad>
hero.lede: Say what you ate and watch it land on a 24-hour dial. Per-gram macros, targets from Mifflin-St Jeor, and a coach that sees the whole day, not just the last meal.
hero.orbitSummary: An example day: 742 kcal left, two meals logged, protein, carbs and fat rings mostly full.
hero.coachChip: You're 54 g short on protein. Chicken tagine would close it.
hero.voiceChip: "200 g chicken, a cup of rice…"

how.title: Say it. See it land. Close the gap.
how.oneExample: "two eggs and a msemen with honey"
how.oneTitle: Say it, snap it or scan it
how.oneBody: Voice, a photo, a barcode or plain text. The coach matches each item to the verified library and shows you the grams before anything is logged.
how.twoBody: Every meal becomes a dot at the time you ate it. The rings for protein, carbs and fat fill up, and the lit arc shows your eating window.
how.threeExample: Your window closes at 20:00, and you're 54 g short. Here are two dinners that fit.
how.threeBody: Because it sees the whole day, its advice is specific: what to eat next, how much of it, and when.

system.title: Numbers you can train on.
system.lede: No estimates, no vibes. One equation, one verified food library, and plans built from the same math your diary runs on.
system.targetsBody: Mifflin-St Jeor BMR, scaled by how often you actually train. Adaptive TDEE then learns from your real weight trend.
system.gramBody: Every food is stored per 100 g. Log 137 g of rice and the maths is exact.
system.plansBody: Cut, maintain or build. Apply a full day to your orbit in one tap, or ask the AI to adapt one for Ramadan, training days or a tight budget.

coach.title: In your corner, grounded in evidence.
coach.lede: It reads your targets, trend and today's orbit, and cites its sources. It won't give medical advice, and it's for adults only.
coach.question: Why am I always hungry at 4pm?
coach.answer: Your lunches average only 22 g of protein, and there's a 5-hour gap before dinner. Try moving 30 g of protein into lunch. Greek yogurt or tuna would do it.
coach.source: Source: evidence brief on protein distribution

targets.a: BMR comes from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, multiplied by your training level to get TDEE. Your goal then sets calories: −500 to lose, +350 to gain, with a floor of 1,200. Once you log your weight, adaptive TDEE refines it from your real trend.

moroccan.a: Yes. The library includes msemen, harira, baghrir, tagines and more, next to thousands of USDA and Open Food Facts entries. You can also add your own foods and recipes.

safe.a: It is adults-only, grounded in cited evidence, and won't give medical advice. Nothing it suggests is logged until you confirm it.

offline.a: Logging queues up while you're offline and syncs when you reconnect. It installs as an app on iOS and Android.

name.a: So3ra is سعرة, "calorie" in Arabic. The 3 is Arabizi shorthand for the letter ع, the way it's typed every day across Morocco.

languages.a: English, French and Arabic, with a proper right-to-left layout.
